text: They would not be free again for twenty-seven years. They were moved from Florida to Alabama, and then to Fort Sill in Oklahoma. In the damp prison camps, disease killed many of them, children most of all. Geronimo himself died at Fort Sill in nineteen-oh-nine, still a prisoner.

The boundaries didn't change. The name did, and so did the attention. The law also requires the Park Service to protect traditional cultural and religious sites, to consult with tribes, and to guarantee access for tribal members, including temporary closures when a tribe asks for privacy. The Chiricahua Apache are still here. Their descendants live today with the Fort Sill Apache Tribe in Oklahoma and at Mescalero in New Mexico, and their connection to these mountains never ended.
A volcano built it. Ice carved it. Warriors defended it, outlaws hid in it, a blind woman kept it, and a jaguar has walked through it.
